newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Electric shrs do not reflect growth outlook-DMG.
newsitem.headline: HK Electric shrs do not reflect growth outlook-DMG.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, which is advising an independent board committee of Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd, said Hutchison Whampoa Ltd's offer for Hongkong Electric did not reflect growth prospects.

"We consider that the offer undervalues HKE (Hongkong Electric) and, accordingly, we do not consider the terms of the offer to be fair and reasonable and advise the independent board committee to recommend that independent shareholders should not accept the offer in respect of their shareholdings in HKE," it said in a report to the committee.
The report was sent to shareholders on Friday.
Hutchison Whampoa is offering HK$26.50 per share for Hongkong Electric shares after it increased its stake to 35.01 percent, triggering a general offer.
"The offer price does not, in our view, reflect the growth prospects of the group," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.

It said the Sino British Joint Liaison Group's endorsement of a renewed Scheme of Control, which governs the financial affairs of the Hongkong Electric Co Ltd, "is significant to the longer term growth prospect of the group".
Developments in Hong Kong also pointed to "a need for an increase in electricity generating capacity", it added.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said Hongkong Electric shares have underperformed the Hang Seng Index. "The effect of this is that the price earnings multiple of HKE is at a discount to the price earnings multiple of the Hang Seng Index," it said.

Based on a company estimate of 1996 net profit of not less than HK$4.15 billion, the offer price represented a PE multiple of about 12.9 times. The Hang Seng index is trading at a multiple of about 18 times, it said.
Hongkong Electric was also trading at a significant discount to other listed power companies in Asia, it added.
The stock closed Friday morning's session down HK$0.25 at HK$26.75

In a letter to shareholders, the independent board committee said it agreed with the view of its financial adviser that the offer undervalued Hongkong Electric and recommended that shareholders should not accept the offer.
